positiveFindings: All 20 event branches compile independently under JSON Schema Draft 2020-12, have one unambiguous valid baseline, and reject every one of 1,522 fresh structural mutations.
Role enum aliases, case changes, trailing spaces, and Unicode confusable role strings are structurally rejected.
FOCUS_ONLY is exactly GRAMMAR_ERROR then BLANK_INFERENCE; ALL_25 is the exact accepted 25-type UI order; reordered, duplicated, short, and long type arrays are rejected.
The accepted type-binding v4 bytes rehash and all eight epoch-1 main/holdout family selections recompute exactly.
The declared 12-state/11-transition chain rejects all 133 nonedges; every state has a nonempty deny set; phase 1 is blind-surface/codebook only; POST_ACTIVATION_RESULT retains five explicit denials.
The declared authorization-open-consume-close order, immediate ordinals/prior hashes, time ordering, and unique one-use capability rules reject 128 fresh stateful chain attacks.
The subject remains empty and design-only: no actor, item, gold, certificate, candidate, audit, grant, result access, evaluator authority, scoring authority, or execution authority exists.

blockers.finding: The exclusion graph compares actorPseudonym strings but defines no one-person/one-pseudonym identity commitment, canonical normalization, or proof record. Both Actor-Pseudonym-0000 and actor-pseudonym-0000 are valid and can hold incompatible author/auditor roles as separate registry identities.
blockers.impact: The same person can be represented by case aliases and audit their own packet, item, gold, certificate, candidate, or activation evidence while every role enum and per-record schema remains valid.
blockers.requiredClosure: Bind each role assignment to a stable privacy-preserving human identity commitment issued once, define exact pseudonym normalization, and require a registry-wide uniqueness/exclusion proof over that commitment rather than raw display pseudonyms.

blockers.finding: PASSED_COVERAGE_EVENT carries an unconstrained slotId and canonicalTypeId but no slot-materialization event hash. Neither the schema nor coverage policy requires that the slot exist, be eligible, be distinct in the map, or have the same phase/type under binding v4.
blockers.impact: Twenty-five distinct PASS events can reuse MC-N-01 while claiming all 25 canonical types, satisfy the per-map-key and unique-event-hash rules, and fabricate ALL_25 from one slot.
blockers.requiredClosure: Bind every pass event to the exact immutable slot-materialization event and decision event; require slot/type/phase equality, eligibility, one terminal pass per slot, and distinct slots for distinct coverage entries.

blockers.finding: The only canonical-event rule hashes event bytes excluding eventSha256. candidateCanonicalBytesSha256 and auditReportCanonicalBytesSha256 are themselves inside those event bytes, but no separate hash domain or exclusion list is defined for either required field.
blockers.impact: Hashing the declared whole event is self-referential; treating the fields as arbitrary also passes. The claimed exact candidate/audit byte binding is therefore not independently reproducible even though the high-level candidate-to-audit-to-grant order is noncircular.
blockers.requiredClosure: Define typed domain-separated canonical payloads that explicitly exclude both digest fields, publish their exact field lists/canonicalization, and bind their recomputed digests in the audit and grant.

blockers.finding: The seven fingerprint values and composite are opaque SHA strings. No normalization version, eight-word-window algorithm, topic/scenario canonicalization, author-identity binding, surface-template derivation, composite formula, or visible-surface recomputation proof exists.
blockers.impact: All 60 slots can commit the identical visible surface while supplying 60 arbitrary unique bundles; the 1,770 pair proof and tombstone checks then report no collision and replay protection is illusory.
blockers.requiredClosure: Specify deterministic versioned fingerprint derivation and composite domains, bind inputs to the item/source/surface/author commitments, and require independent recomputation before reservation, materialization, disjointness proof, and tombstone comparison.

blockers.finding: Authorization records actorRole, but each policy row defines only phase, state, resource allow/deny lists, and optional precondition. No row defines which roles may access its allowlisted resources.
blockers.impact: A PACKET_AUTHOR can structurally receive TRUSTED_GOLD_AUDIT_BUNDLE during the independent gold audit, and 100 analogous wrong-role authorizations remain admissible across the seven rows.
blockers.requiredClosure: Add exact allowed-role sets per phase-state-resource tuple, bind their digest in authorization and denial proofs, and reject an actor whose stable identity lacks the exact active role assignment.

blockers.finding: ACTIVATION_GRANT sets authorityGranted and resultAccessAuthorized true but has no policyMatrixSha256, allowlistSha256, denySetSha256, resourceClassPolicyProofSha256, stateTransitionEvidenceSha256, or policy-registry-ready binding. The state transition also names no such required seal.
blockers.impact: A syntactically valid grant can be issued while policyRegistry.ready is false, contradicting the package's explicit claim that an empty policy registry cannot support a grant and leaving result-access scope dependent on an opaque deterministicGrantProofSha256.
blockers.requiredClosure: Require the grant to bind the exact sealed nonempty policy registry, POST_ACTIVATION_RESULT allow/deny roots, role policy, scope proof, and transition proof; reject empty/zero/unresolved policy evidence before authority or result access becomes true.
